messages:
alex: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout I see an increase in tail latency for host-side short-chat requests (seq <= 128). p50 35ms, p95 210ms, p99 460ms. before rollout p99 ~200ms. suspect host parse + tokenization + a kernel mismatch causing extra copies. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

maria: saw the same in the canary dashboards at ~03:10 UTC. spike correlates with a rise in parse CPU and grpc write stalls. KV cache hitrate for these requests dropped ~12% around the same time.

priya: looks like kernel chooser now prefers the `wide-attn` kernels for small sequences because of a heuristic change. those kernels have a different batching interaction and increase preparse cost per-request. we should either revert the chooser for seq<=128 or tweak batching heuristics.

sam: ran a quick flamegraph on the canary instance. top stacks (sample):

`````
parse_request              35%  // utf8 normalize, header parse
tokenize_stream            22%  // host tokenizer, buffer copies
kernel_select              18%  // chooser + metadata gather
grpc_write                 10%  // smallwrite stalls
kvcache_lookup             08%  // misses + fallback

```

repro command I used: `perf record -F 99 -g -- /srv/redwood/host-runtime --canary`

alex: thanks — that mirrors my trace. interesting that kvcache misses coincided. could be the new kernel order changes request batching order which impacts KV locality.

maria: confirmed with trace correlation: when batcher groups mixed-length requests the kv cache sees more cross-request key churn -> lower hitrate -> extra latency. i captured a short log snippet of two requests that got coalesced:

`````
[INFO] req=abcd seq=64 kkeys=[k1,k2] -> kvcache MISS
[INFO] req=efgh seq=1024 kkeys=[k1,k3] -> kvcache HIT

```

coalesced -> k1 evicted between them.

priya: quick mitigation options:
- revert kernel chooser for seq<=128 (fast rollback)
- make batcher avoid mixing short (<128) + long (>512) requests in same batch
- add cheap kvcache-prefetch for predicted keys when batch is heterogeneous

i can push config canary for the second option (batch split) today.

sam: +1 for batch split as low-risk. also propose adding a metric: `kernel_variant_by_seqlen` and `kvcache_hitrate_by_seqlen` so we can monitor before/after.

alex: agreed. for immediate rollback i'll pin canary to previous kernel variant until we validate batch-split. @ci-bot can you deploy a rollback to canary 7999991200?

ci-bot: runbook triggered: deploying canary pin -> image: host-runtime:v1.42.7-pin-oldkernel. started at 7999995020. will report status. :rocket:

maria: small repro curl to run locally if you want to see the parse+tokenize overhead:

`````
curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"short chat hello"}' \
  https://canary.api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate?model=redwood-small

watch `top`/`perf` while running 200 req/s. you'll see tokenize_stream spikes.

priya: pushed batch-split config to canary cluster (split_short_and_long: true, short_threshold_tokens: 128). also enabled a debug trace for kvcache evictions for 1h.

sam: after batch-split push, early signal: p99 reduced from 460ms -> 240ms on canary (rough), kv hitrate for short-seq improved ~9%. not fully back to baseline but better.

alex: plan: keep pin for canary until we have 24h of telemetry with batch-split enabled. if stable, roll kernel-selection change with adaptive batch-split turned on by default. action items:
- priya: monitor kvcache evictions by seqlen, enable alert if >5% regression (ASAP)
- sam: add kernel_variant_by_seqlen metric + dashboard (today)
- maria: coordinate canary telemetry + perf traces for next 24h
- alex: approve rollback pin until metrics green

priya: on it. i'll also prepare a small change to the chooser: add a cheap fast-path for seq<=128 that avoids collecting heavy metadata (should shave ~6-8ms).

sam: logged issue #INV-4821 with perf traces and flamegraphs attached.

alex: thanks team. follow-ups in #postmortems if regression persists. :thumbsup:
